items.title: ROS Discourse General: Nvidia jetson debloating guide
items.summary: A user is seeking a guide for debloating the Nvidia Jetson, specifically to remove unnecessary bloat from the JetPack release. The user could not find existing comprehensive guides for this process. They have documented the steps they took for cleaning up the system. The user is offering to write up their documentation into a free blog post. They are seeking interest from others who might be interested in such a guide.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Nvidia jetson debloating guide". This segment details a user's process for removing unnecessary bloat from the Nvidia Jetson, resulting in a documented method for system cleanup. The user sought guidance on debloating the Nvidia Jetson and documented the steps taken to clean up the system, offering to publish this documentation publicly. The methodology involved a self-documented process to reduce the footprint of the JetPack release by removing extraneous components. This effort provides a potentially useful resource for other users managing Jetson hardware and software environments. The availability of such guides is important for optimizing resource utilization in artificial intelligence and edge computing applications.

items.title: Cyborg roaches to the rescue?
items.summary: Researchers developed a diving suit and oxygen generation system for Madagascar hissing cockroaches to enable underwater and low-oxygen survival. These cyborg insects are guided remotely and can navigate environments like floods, rubble, and drains for up to three hours. They have already demonstrated utility by deploying with infrared cameras during an earthquake to identify signs of life. This capability suggests a greater potential for assisting in underwater search-and-rescue operations. Other biohybrids, such as bionic jellyfish and muscle-powered robots, are also being explored by various research groups.
items.audio_script: From thehustle.co, "Cyborg roaches to the rescue?". This report details the development of a diving suit and oxygen generation system for Madagascar hissing cockroaches enabling underwater and low-oxygen survival. Researchers have engineered these cyborg insects to navigate environments such as floods, rubble, and drains for periods up to three hours through remote guidance. The insects have demonstrated utility by deploying with infrared cameras during an earthquake to successfully identify signs of life in obscured locations. This capability suggests a potential application in assisting underwater search-and-rescue operations. Other biohybrids, including bionic jellyfish and muscle-powered robots, are currently under investigation by various research groups. This advancement indicates further exploration of biohybrid systems for complex environmental interaction.
